description: CPU engine decode vs QWEN_THREADS on Apple M5 (ADR 0013 parallel projections). bench --backend vector --decode-steps 32 --warmup 1 --runs 3, 4-token prompt [16,10,16,28].
hardware: Apple M5 (4 performance + 6 efficiency cores), 16 GB, macOS 27.3
note: 40 tok/s x 1.5 GB of BF16 weights per token is about 60 GB/s, well below the ~130 GB/s the GPU reaches; unlike the Ryzen 9 9900X (WSL2, ~41 GB/s, flat from 2 threads) the M5 keeps scaling up to the 6th thread. Results are bit-identical for every thread count (ADR 0013).

bf16_vs_f32_host_storage_decode_tok_s.method: same commit; the f32 variant widened BF16 tensors to an f32 host copy at load (scratch build, not committed), i.e. the pre-ADR 0012 storage with the ADR 0013 parallel kernels. Same model identity.

metal_bf16_vs_f32_device_weights.input: 454-token prompt, 64 new tokens, chunk 128, 2 runs each
